title: SIESTA as a universal unbiased proteomics approach for identification and prioritization of enzyme substrates
protocol: Culture cells in multiple 175 cm² flasks (Sarstedt).
Detach cultured cells with trypsinization and wash twice with PBS.
Resuspend detached cells in 12 mL of 50 mM HEPES pH 7.5, containing complete protease inhibitor cocktail and phosphatase inhibitor tablets.
Lyse resuspended cells by five freeze-thaw cycles using liquid nitrogen in multiple 1.5 mL eppendorfs.
Centrifuge the cell lysate at 21,000 g for 10 minutes at 4°C.
Measure protein concentration in the lysate using BCA assay.
Distribute the lysate equally into 8 aliquots (1.1-1.2 mL each).
Treat each pair of aliquots with vehicle, 500 µM ATP, 500 nM AKT1 or with AKT1+ATP and incubate on a thermomixer at 37°C for 30 minutes.
After incubation, aliquot each replicate into 10 PCR microtubes (100 μL each).
Incubate each microtube in the thermocycler at corresponding temperature points of 37, 41, 44, 47, 50, 53, 56, 59, 63, and 67°C for 3 minutes.
Let the samples cool down for 3 minutes at room temperature and afterwards keep on ice.
Transfer the samples into polycarbonate thickwall tubes and centrifuge at 100,000 g and 4°C for 20 minutes.
After ultracentrifugation, collect the soluble protein fractions and transfer them to new Eppendorf tubes.
Measure protein concentration in the samples treated at lowest temperature points (37 and 41°C) using BCA Assay.
Determine the volume containing 50 µg of protein in the samples corresponding to 37 and 41°C.
Transfer the same volume from each sample to new Eppendorf tubes.
Add urea to the final concentration of 4 M.
Add DTT to a final concentration of 10 mM and incubate for 1 hour at room temperature.
Add IAA to a final concentration of 50 mM.
Incubate for 1 hour at room temperature in the dark.
Quench the reaction by adding an additional 10 mM of DTT.
Add 4 volumes of methanol to the samples and vortex.
Add 1 volume of chloroform to the samples and vortex.
Add 3 volumes of deionized water to the samples.
Centrifuge the samples at 21,000 g for 10 minutes.
Discard the aqueous layer above the pellet as much as possible.
Add 1 volume of methanol, disrupt the pellet by pipetting.
Wash the pellet by centrifugation at 21,000 g for 10 minutes.
Discard the supernatant.
Let the pellets dry (but do not over-dry the pellets).
Dissolve the semi-dry protein pellet in 20 mM EPPS (pH=8.5) with 8 M urea.
Dilute urea to 4 M.
Dissolve LysC in 20 mM EPPS, add 1:100 w/w enzyme to protein.
Incubate the samples at room temperature overnight.
Dilute the urea to 1 M.
Dissolve sequencing-grade trypsin in 20 mM EPPS and add 1:100 w/w enzyme to protein.
Incubate the samples at room temperature for 6 hours.
Add acetonitrile to a final concentration of 20%.
Dissolve TMT10 reagents and add 4x by weight to the samples (200 μg TMT label for 50 μg of protein).
Incubate the samples for 2 h at room temperature.
Quench the reaction by addition of 0.5% hydroxylamine for 15 min at room temperature.
Pool the labeled samples from each replicate.
Dry at least 30% of the samples to reduce the acetonitrile content to <5%.
Acidify the samples to pH 1-3 using TFA.
Clean the samples using Sep-Pak cartridges, according to the manufacturer protocol.
Dry the samples using DNA 120 SpeedVac concentrator.
Dissolve each replicate in 0.1% TFA and fractionate into 8 fractions using Pierce High pH Reversed-Phase Peptide Fractionation Kit.
Or: Resuspend the samples in 20 mM ammonium hydroxide and fractionate into 96 fractions on an XBridge BEH C18 2.1x150 mm column, using a Dionex Ultimate 3000 LC system.
Dry the samples in a concentrator.
Store peptide pellets at -80°C.
Dissolve the samples in buffer A to an estimated concentration of 0.2 μg/μl.
Prepare liquid chromatograph (Dionex UltiMate 3000 UHPLC system).
Prepare buffer A (0.1% formic acid and 2% acetonitrile in water) and buffer B (0.1% formic acid, 98% acetonitrile in water).
Load 5 μL of each sample.
Perform reverse-phase separation using an Easy-Spray HPLC column (75 µm internal diameter, packed with PepMap C18, 2 µm beads, 100 Å pore size).
Connect the EASY-Spray column to a nanoflow Dionex UltiMate 3000 UHPLC system.
Elute in an organic solvent gradient increasing from 4% to 26% (B: 98% acetonitrile, 0.1% formic acid, 2% water) at a flow rate of 300 nL min\(^{-1}\) over 95 min.
Program the Q Exactive HF method to record precursor ion spectra at m/z 375-1500 with 120,000 m/z resolution.
Set automatic gain control target to 3x10^6 ions and maximum injection time of 100 ms for precursor ion spectra recording.
Record fragment ions in MS/MS mode with 60,000 m/z resolution.
Set automatic gain control target to 2 x10^5 ions and maximum injection time of 120 ms for MS/MS recording.
Process mass spectra raw files using MaxQuant (e.g., v. 1.5.6.5 or 1.6.2.3).
Use UniProt complete human proteome database for protein identification.
Specify Trypsin/P as enzyme specificity and allow no more than 2 missed cleavages.
Select TMT10-plex in MS2 for peptide quantification.
Set cysteine carbamidomethylation as a fixed modification.
Include methionine oxidation as a variable modification.
Add phosphorylation on serine and threonine as variable modifications.
Use the same settings in quantification if AKT1 is used as an enzyme.
Filter results at both protein and peptide levels with a 1% false discovery rate.
Analyze "ProteinGroups.txt" file using SIESTA package hosted on GitHub.
